newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay High oil output up 20,000 bbls per day.
newsitem.headline: Bombay High oil output up 20,000 bbls per day.

text.p: Oil output from Bombay High, India's largest oilfield, has risen by about 20,000 barrels per day this month compared to May 1996 levels, the chairman of Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) said on Thursday.

"Bombay High production is already coming up," ONGC chairman and managing director Bikash Bora, told reporters, in reply to a question after addressing an international seminar on deep sea exploration technology.
"It has risen in the last six months," he said.
He said production levels this month were higher by about 20,000 barrels per day compared to May 1996 levels.
He said ONGC had deliberately cut down production at some wells for repairs and related work.
Bombay High fields contribute the bulk of India's oil production. ONGC is India's leading oil and gas producer.
